item.title: Cisco Catalyst 3560 IOS Upgrade: Two Methods and Verification
item.description: Upgrading IOS on a Cisco Catalyst 3560 — archive download-sw versus manual copy and boot system, flash space, MD5 verification and rollback.
item.content:encoded:
Upgrading IOS on a Catalyst 3560 is not complicated, but the details matter: which file format you download, how much space is left in flash, and whether the boot variable points to the right image. A mistake in any of these leaves you with a switch that boots into the boot loader instead of IOS.

There are two ways to do it:

  • Method A: archive download-sw with a .tar file. The switch extracts the image, the web device manager files and sets the boot variable itself.
  • Method B: manual upgrade with a .bin file. You copy the image, verify it, set boot system and reload.

Lab note: I am upgrading my own Catalyst 3560 8-port PoE switch with both methods. Console outputs and timings from that lab will be added to this guide.

1. Before You Start

Back Up the Configuration

Switch# copy running-config startup-config
Switch# copy startup-config tftp:

Keep the backup off the switch: on your laptop, a TFTP or SCP server, or your configuration management tool.

Identify the Model, Version and Feature Set

Switch# show version
Switch# show inventory

Write down three things:

  • Exact model, for example WS-C3560-8PC-S. The image must match the platform.
  • Current IOS version.
  • Feature set, for example IP Base (ipbasek9) or IP Services (ipservicesk9). Choose the same feature set for the new image unless you deliberately change it.

Check the Boot Settings and Flash Space

Switch# show boot
Switch# dir flash:

show boot shows which image the switch loads at the next reload. dir flash: shows the files and, at the bottom, the free space. Compact switches like the 8-port 3560 have little flash. Often there is not enough room for two images at the same time.

Download the Image

Download the image from Cisco Software Download. A service contract is required. You will find two file types:

File Contents Used with
.tar IOS image plus web device manager files archive download-sw (Method A)
.bin IOS image only Manual copy and boot system (Method B)

Note the MD5 checksum shown on the download page. You will compare it on the switch.

The classic Catalyst 3560 is end of life, so the latest release on the download page is the final one for this platform.

2. Method A: archive download-sw

This is the method Cisco recommends for this switch family. One command transfers the .tar file, extracts it into a new directory in flash, updates the boot variable and optionally reloads.

Switch# archive download-sw /overwrite /reload tftp://192.0.2.10/c3560-ipservicesk9-tar.<version>.tar

The most useful options:

Option Effect
/overwrite Replaces the current image if there is not enough space for both
/leave-old-sw Keeps the old image (only if flash has room for both)
/reload Reloads the switch after a successful download
/imageonly Installs only the IOS image, without the web device manager files

If you have room for both images, use /leave-old-sw instead of /overwrite. Rollback is then just a boot variable change.

Without /reload, check the result before reloading:

Switch# show boot
Switch# dir flash:
Switch# reload

3. Method B: Manual Upgrade with a .bin File

The manual method gives you full control over each step. It is useful when you only have a .bin file, or when you want to verify the image before touching the boot variable.

Copy the Image

Switch# copy tftp://192.0.2.10/c3560-ipservicesk9-mz.<version>.bin flash:

If there is not enough space, you must delete the old image first. That removes your rollback option on the switch, so make sure you have the old image on your TFTP server and a console connection ready.

TFTP works for small files but is slow and unreliable over long distances. If your IOS version supports it, SCP or FTP is faster.

Verify the Checksum

Switch# verify /md5 flash:c3560-ipservicesk9-mz.<version>.bin

Compare the result with the MD5 value from the Cisco download page. If they differ, delete the file and copy it again. Never boot an image that failed verification.

Set the Boot Variable and Reload

Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# boot system flash:c3560-ipservicesk9-mz.<version>.bin
Switch(config)# end
Switch# copy running-config startup-config
Switch# show boot
Switch# reload

Check show boot before the reload. The BOOT path-list must point to the new image, with the correct file name and path.

4. After the Upgrade

Switch# show version
Switch# show interfaces status
Switch# show power inline
Switch# show logging
  • show version: the new IOS version is running.
  • show interfaces status: all expected ports are up.
  • show power inline: PoE devices are powered again.
  • show logging: no errors during boot.

When you are sure the new version works, remove the old image to free up space, unless you want to keep it for rollback.

5. Rollback

  • Old image still in flash: point the boot variable back to it with boot system flash:<old-image>, save and reload.
  • Old image deleted: copy it back from your TFTP server, verify the MD5 and set the boot variable.
  • Switch does not boot IOS at all: it stops at the switch: prompt. This is covered in When a Catalyst 3560 Won’t Boot: Recovery from the Boot Loader.

Common Mistakes

  • Wrong platform or feature set. An image for another model does not boot.
  • Deleting the old image before the new one is verified. If the copy is corrupted, you have nothing to boot.
  • A typo in boot system. The switch cannot find the image and stops at the boot loader.
  • No console connection during the reload. If something goes wrong, you can only see it from the console.

item.title: Cisco Nexus NX-OS Software Upgrade Guide: Field-Tested Step by Step
item.description: Field-tested guide for upgrading Cisco Nexus NX-OS — preparation, upgrade path, file transfer, rollback, and ROMMON recovery scenarios.
item.content:encoded:
This guide covers the Cisco Nexus NX-OS software upgrade process in a practical, step-by-step manner — including rollback and recovery scenarios. The goal is to minimize service disruption and ensure the device can always be recovered in case of failure.

Most upgrade failures are not caused by the upgrade itself — they are caused by skipping preparation steps. This guide treats preparation as seriously as execution.

For out-of-band access during upgrade failures, see: The Backdoor of the Network: Next-Gen Console Server Architecture

1. Pre-Upgrade Checks

Before starting the software upgrade, you must complete the preparation steps below. This phase is the most commonly skipped — and the most common source of problems.

Configuration Backup

  • Take a backup of the current configuration before anything else.
  • Store the backup on your own computer or an external location such as FTP/SFTP — not on the switch itself.
  • If the upgrade fails or a rollback is needed, this backup is critical.

Verify Switch Model and Current Software Version

Check the switch model and the running NX-OS version with these commands:

show version
show module
show inventory

These outputs are required to select the correct NX-OS image, determine the upgrade path, and verify hardware compatibility.

2. Download the Software Image

  • Download the correct NX-OS image for your switch model from Cisco’s official portal: https://software.cisco.com/download/home
  • A valid Cisco account with the appropriate entitlements is required.
  • After downloading, note the MD5 hash value — you will need it to verify file integrity after transfer.

MD5 verification confirms the file was not corrupted during download. This step is not optional.

3. Verify the Upgrade Path

A direct upgrade from your current NX-OS version to the target version is not always supported. Some version combinations require intermediate steps.

Use Cisco’s official tools to verify:

  • Nexus Upgrade Matrix Tools
  • Nexus 9000 / 3000 Series
  • Nexus 7000 Series

If multiple upgrade steps are required, download all intermediate images before starting the process.

4. Copy the Software File to the Switch

Option A: FTP Transfer

FTP is one of the most common methods. Note that NX-OS images can be close to 2 GB, so transfer time depends on network speed.

Example:

copy ftp://user1:Qazwsx@10.10.10.5/nxos.9.3.10.bin bootflash:

If multiple VRFs are configured on the Nexus, you will be asked which VRF to use for the transfer. Since the management interface typically uses the management VRF, select management VRF.

Option B: USB Transfer (Recommended)

USB transfer is my preferred method when:

  • No FTP server is readily available
  • You have time constraints
  • You want to avoid any network transfer risk
copy usb1:nxos.9.3.10.bin bootflash:

Ensure the USB filesystem format is supported by the Nexus device before proceeding.

MD5 Hash Verification

After the transfer, verify file integrity:

show file bootflash:nxos.9.3.10.bin md5sum

The output must exactly match the MD5 hash from the Cisco download portal.

5. Run the Upgrade

Once all checks are complete, start the upgrade:

install all nxos bootflash:nxos.9.3.10.bin
  • The switch automatically saves the current configuration before installation.
  • You will be prompted for confirmation before the reboot.
  • After confirmation, the device reboots and the upgrade begins.

Upgrade duration varies depending on the device model and software size.

6. Rollback and Recovery Scenarios

ROMMON Mode Entry

If the installation fails or the device does not boot:

  • During device startup, press CTRL + L or CTRL + C via console connection to enter ROMMON mode.

Boot via TFTP from ROMMON

set ip 10.10.10.2 255.255.255.0
set gw 10.10.10.1
cmdline recoverymode=1
boot tftp://10.10.10.2/tftpboot/nxos.9.3.10.bin
init system
reload-nxos

Boot via USB from ROMMON

boot usb1:nxos.9.3.10.bin bootflash:
set ip 10.10.10.2 255.255.255.0
set gw 10.10.10.1
cmdline recoverymode=1
boot usb1:nxos.9.3.10.bin
init system
reload-nxos

After booting from TFTP or USB, verify and correct the boot settings:

show boot

configure terminal
  boot nxos bootflash:/nxos.9.3.10.bin

Critical Warning

During the software upgrade:

  • Do not interrupt the network connection
  • Do not interrupt the power supply

Either condition can render the device unrecoverable without physical intervention.
